sources.title: Energy consumption model for sensor nodes based on LoRa and LoRaWAN

establishes.statement: Wireless communication has an energy cost that this paper's authors describe as far higher, at TinyML's scale, than the cost of on-device compute.
establishes.support_quote: "avoiding the energy cost associated with wireless communication, which at this scale is far higher than that of compute [5]"

sources.why_useful: Grounds the Introduction's claim that on-device inference saves energy relative to transmission.

sources.title: Exploring CoreMark, a benchmark maximizing simplicity and efficacy

establishes.statement: CoreMark is the standard MCU-class benchmark but does not profile full programs or represent ML inference workloads.
establishes.support_quote: "CoreMark does not profile full programs, nor does it accurately represent machine learning inference workloads."

sources.why_useful: Anchors one arm of the Gap (closest prior benchmark that is not ML-representative).

sources.title: MLPerf Inference Benchmark

establishes.statement: MLPerf's inference benchmark suite excludes MCUs and other resource-constrained platforms for lack of small benchmarks and compatible implementations.
establishes.support_quote: "the current MLPerf inference benchmark precludes MCUs and other resource-constrained platforms due to a lack of small benchmarks and compatible implementations."

sources.why_useful: Anchors the third arm of the Gap and situates MLPerf Tiny within the broader MLPerf effort.

sources.title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context

establishes.statement: MSCOCO 2014 is the source dataset preprocessed to build the Visual Wake Words benchmark.
establishes.support_quote: "The Visual Wakewords Challenge uses the MSCOCO 2014 dataset [15] as the training, validation and test datasets for all person detection models."

sources.why_useful: Names the origin of the VWW benchmark's image data.

sources.title: Visual Wake Words Dataset

establishes.statement: The Visual Wake Words challenge is a person-detection task built for microcontroller-class deployment, which MLPerf Tiny adopts as its VWW benchmark.
establishes.support_quote: "The Visual Wakewords challenge [6] tasked submitters with detecting whether at least one person is in an image...the reference network provided as part of the challenge fits on most 32-bit embedded microcontrollers."

sources.why_useful: Names the origin of the VWW task and its reference model.

sources.title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications

establishes.statement: MobileNetV1 (with a width multiplier alpha) is the architecture family used as the VWW reference model.
establishes.support_quote: "The Visual Wakewords model is a MobilenetV1 [11] which takes 96x96 input images with an alpha of 0.25 and two output classes"

sources.why_useful: Names the VWW reference model architecture.

establishes.statement: CIFAR-10 is a 60,000-image, 10-class labeled subset of the 80 Million Tiny Images dataset, used as the image-classification benchmark's dataset.
establishes.support_quote: "CIFAR-10 [14] is a labeled subset of the 80 Million Tiny Images dataset [20]."

sources.title: Sparse: Sparse Architecture Search for CNNs on Resource-Constrained Microcontrollers
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS)

establishes.statement: Prior TinyML work has used CIFAR-10 as a target dataset, which MLPerf Tiny's authors cite as part of their reason for keeping CIFAR-10 in the suite.
establishes.support_quote: "A significant amount of prior work in TinyML has used CIFAR-10 as a target dataset [8]"

sources.why_useful: Supports the design-rationale claim for keeping CIFAR-10 as a historical point of reference.

sources.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
sources.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)

establishes.statement: ResNet is the official architecture family that the IC benchmark's custom, smaller reference model (ResNetv1) is adapted from.
establishes.support_quote: "The Image Classification model is a customized ResNetv1 [10] which takes 32x32x3 input images"

sources.why_useful: Names the architecture family the IC reference model modifies.

sources.title: Speech Commands: A Dataset for Limited-Vocabulary Speech Recognition

establishes.statement: Speech Commands v2 is the dataset underlying the keyword-spotting benchmark.
establishes.support_quote: "We used the Speech Commands v2 dataset[21], a collection of 105,829 utterances collected from 2,618 speakers with a variety of accents."

sources.title: Hello Edge: Keyword Spotting on Microcontrollers

establishes.statement: This paper describes the small depthwise-separable CNN that MLPerf Tiny adopts as its KWS closed-division reference model.
establishes.support_quote: "For the closed division model, we used the small depthwise-separable CNN described in [22]. We chose this model because with 38.6K parameters, it fits within the available memory of most microcontrollers"

sources.why_useful: Names the origin of the KWS reference model.

sources.title: ToyADMOS: A Dataset of Miniature-Machine Operating Sounds for Anomalous Sound Detection
sources.venue: IEEE Workshop on Applications of Signal Processing to Audio and Acoustics (WASPAA)

establishes.statement: ToyADMOS is one of the two source datasets combined into DCASE2020, which underlies the anomaly-detection benchmark.
establishes.support_quote: "the dataset from the DCASE2020 [13] competition, which is itself a combination of two publicly available sources: the ToyADMOS [12], and the MIMII [17] datasets."

sources.why_useful: Names one source dataset behind the AD benchmark.

sources.title: MIMII Dataset: Sound Dataset for Malfunctioning Industrial Machine Investigation and Inspection

establishes.statement: MIMII is the second source dataset combined into DCASE2020.
establishes.support_quote: "a combination of two publicly available sources: the ToyADMOS [12], and the MIMII [17] datasets."

sources.why_useful: Names the second source dataset behind the AD benchmark.

sources.title: Description and Discussion on DCASE2020 Challenge Task2: Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection for Machine Condition Monitoring

establishes.statement: DCASE2020 Task 2 is the competition whose dataset and reference autoencoder MLPerf Tiny adapted for its anomaly-detection benchmark.
establishes.support_quote: "we have selected to use the dataset from the DCASE2020 [13] competition...we have selected the AE based model also used in the reference implementation of DCASE2020"

sources.why_useful: Names the competition whose dataset and reference model the AD benchmark reuses.

sources.title: MicroNets: Neural Network Architectures for Deploying TinyML Applications on Commodity Microcontrollers
sources.venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems, 3

establishes.statement: MLPerf Tiny's benchmarks have already acted as a standard task set for later TinyML research, including this paper.
establishes.support_quote: "The benchmarks have already acted as a standard set of tasks for TinyML research [4]"

sources.title: Instruction Sets Should Be Free: The Case for RISC-V
sources.venue: EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley, Tech. Rep. UCB/EECS-2014-146

establishes.statement: RISC-V is introduced as a free, open instruction-set architecture, named by the paper when describing the round's RISC-V MCU submission.
establishes.support_quote: "RISC-V is a free, open standard instruction set architecture (ISA) [3]"

sources.why_useful: Backs the one-clause gloss of RISC-V given to an audience that may not know embedded ISA politics.

sources.title: TensorFlow Lite Micro: Embedded Machine Learning on TinyML Systems

establishes.statement: TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) is the runtime used to execute every MLPerf Tiny reference implementation.
establishes.support_quote: "using TFLite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) [7] on the NUCLEO-L4R5ZI board"

sources.why_useful: Names the runtime referenced throughout the Method section; supports the one-clause gloss given to readers unfamiliar with TFLM.
